macro.regime: Hawkish-Fed caution into FOMC minutes week
macro.narrative: Equities closed Friday's session on a soft note heading into the weekend -- the S&P 500 fell 0.40% to 7561.67, the Nasdaq underperformed at -0.91% to 25136.27 even as the Dow eked out a +0.10% gain to 52347.55, and the VIX jumped 3.21% to an elevated 19.30. Asia closed mixed, with the Nikkei the lone gainer (+0.53% to 61142.35) while Hang Seng (-1.55%), STI (-0.96%) and KOSPI (-0.98%) all fell, and Tencent (-3.06%) and Xiaomi (-3.74%) led a sympathetic HK-tech selloff. Gold held flat near $3,886/oz (+0.03%) and silver gave back 1.70% to $49.12, while Brent/WTI near $95.84/$88.56 kept energy's backdrop stable; bitcoin has slipped to roughly $65,311, meaningfully below its recent highs, the cleanest real-time read on risk appetite into this week. The week's center of gravity is Wednesday's FOMC minutes (03:00 SGT) alongside a dense Fed-speaker calendar (Barr, Williams, Warsh, Waller, Hammack, Kashkari, Goolsbee, Barkin, Cook), bookended by Tuesday's US retail sales (decelerating consensus of 0.2%/0.4% vs last month's 0.8%/0.9%), China's October activity data releasing this morning, and Thursday/Friday's Philly Fed, claims and UoM sentiment revision -- a data-dense week that should sharpen rather than resolve the market's current hawkish-but-uncertain Fed-path debate.
